scope: Authorized follow-up cancellation, stale retry and original-result recovery; truthful batch-event presentation.

productionChanges.ui: Cancellation notice is based only on current work.status. latestFollowUp.state=cancelled is labelled as the work-associated continuation; other states identify the shared batch event. No styles, dates, callbacks, ownership, DTOs or ledger changes.
productionChanges.instructions: read_work and read_background_result distinguish batch completion from individual execution; cancelled can also be a stale-constituent overlay on a still-queued batch.

coreFinal.revision: Passed before the final cancelled-overlay text branch and short instruction/contract clarification. Reused by explicit root direction; these checks were not rerun after that text-only review revision.

serverTypecheck.revision: Passed before the final cancelled-overlay text branch and short instruction/contract clarification. Reused by explicit root direction; these checks were not rerun after that text-only review revision.

frontendTypecheck.revision: Passed before the final cancelled-overlay text branch and short instruction/contract clarification. Reused by explicit root direction; these checks were not rerun after that text-only review revision.

coverage: Real saveWork/syncFollowUp/checkDue records and queues due work; cancellation disables it. Recreated stores/worker, two original-job redeliveries and next-day scheduler check produce no worker run or generation.
Two works in one event; one cancelled before generation is absent from current input and provider context. Remaining work generates once, original run and receipt retained on redelivery.

Completed run result persisted before event settlement is reconciled after worker recreation. An expired original claim becomes unknown on redelivery. Neither path creates another run or generates again.

React static render of real work card and view models shows current cancellation before separately labelled batch status, preserves the original event object and cannot infer the cancellation order. Active work also receives batch-event labelling.

The cancelled-overlay render case preserves the underlying queued batch, separately labels the work-associated continuation and tests both cancelled work and waiting work with an obsolete link; neither becomes a claim that the batch or waiting work itself is cancelled.

boundaries.real: Work and continuation stores, run claim/get/finish, family access, encryption, online changes, worker, ProductAgent, ADK Runner/runtime and AI usage store.
boundaries.synthetic: Exact-query rollback-capable Pool, scheduler/job state, Date clock and model provider. UI native-control primitives are stand-ins.
boundaries.modelBudget: No real model or embedding requests. Existing authorized real-model batch remains 20/20 consumed; no reset.

retainedApiCounterexample.scenario: A is cancelled before provider generation; only B executes; completed batch event is then projected to A.latestFollowUp.state.
retainedApiCounterexample.cause: latestAgentWorkFollowUps only projects stale constituents to cancelled while the event is queued. Terminal state remains the original batch outcome.
retainedApiCounterexample.reproduction: After the completed result text assertion in the merged-event test, readWork(cancelledWork.id) and assert latestFollowUp.state === cancelled. This intentionally fails against unchanged server logic.
retainedApiCounterexample.decision: Preserve original API/event values and disclose batch identity in UI and tool contract. There is no durable per-constituent execution/cancellation outcome; do not infer timing from mutable work.updatedAt or rewrite prior completed history. UI green does not resolve or supersede this API counterexample.

retainedUiRed.failure: The baseline cancelled work card lacks the explicit cancellation notice. The UI-only fix makes both render cases pass.

setupNotes: An initial typecheck launch used the parent cwd, so its guard and output paths were unresolved and TypeScript did not run. Correct source-cwd Server and frontend commands subsequently passed. This is a launch error, not a product regression.
notVerified: Real PostgreSQL locking/concurrency, dual processes, actual hard-kill or restart persistence
Cloud Tasks, Scheduler, Firestore, scale-to-zero, cross-store fencing or production bootstrap
Real model understanding, semantic authorization or outside notifications
Browser geometry, screen-reader behavior, live preview, Android or production deployment
Per-constituent executed/omitted outcome or cancellation ordering
publication: Existing v65 reproducible preview source is unavailable; no replacement preview, publish, deployment, PR or merge performed.
